description:
Found 2026-08-14 when the maintainer asked whether https://inis.iaea.org/records/9cr77-d5t43 could be placed under open/. It is ALREADY there, and by this workspace's own rule it should not be.

THE DOCUMENT. Choo, A. J. Y. and Xiao, S. (2023), 'Criticality Analysis of HTR-10 Using the High-Temperature Gas-Cooled Reactor Code Package', VINANST-15, INIS-VN-006, INIS record 9cr77-d5t43.

WHAT WAS CHECKED, 2026-08-14:
- The PDF contains NO copyright, licence, rights or permission statement anywhere. Full-text grep for copyright/(c)/all rights/licen/reproduc/permission returns nothing.
- The INIS record page states 'Copyright (c) 2026 International Atomic Energy Agency. All rights reserved.' Its 'open access' marking means freely READABLE, not freely redistributable.
- The files ARE tracked in git: crates/kovan-literature/open/papers/choo-htr10-criticality.{pdf,json}, added in 89100a934a, and origin is the PUBLIC github.com/theodoreOnzGit/outram-park-backend.

WHY THIS IS THE WRONG TIER, per CLAUDE.md verbatim: 'Decide the access tier BEFORE cataloguing, from the document's own copyright page -- not from where it was downloaded. Public hosting (INIS, gen-4.org, a lab's website) grants no redistribution rights. Unsure means proprietary; that failure direction is recoverable and the other is a licence violation in a public repository.' No statement in the document means unsure, which means proprietary. INIS is named explicitly as granting nothing.

The catalogue entry ALREADY SAYS SO in its own provenance note -- 'No licence statement in the document -- cite and use; do not assume redistribution rights beyond the INIS public copy' -- and the file was filed as open regardless. The note and the placement contradict each other.

A SECOND, SEPARATE INCONSISTENCY. The same document exists twice under different tiers and different years: open/papers/choo-htr10-criticality.{json,pdf} (tracked) versus generated/markdown/proprietary/choo2024criticality.{md,json} and generated/bibtex/proprietary/choo2024criticality.bib (untracked, and under the extractor's wrong 2024 guess). Deduplicate whichever way the tier decision lands.

MAINTAINER DECISION NEEDED, NOT AN AGENT FIX. Removing a tracked PDF from a published repository does not remove it from git history, so 'just move it' is not a complete remedy and the choice of remedy is the maintainer's. Note also that the authors are the maintainer's supervisor (Xiao) and a former colleague (Choo), so PERMISSION MAY WELL EXIST -- it simply is not recorded anywhere. Asking them and recording the grant in the catalogue entry would resolve this in the open direction, legitimately.

OPTIONS: (a) obtain and record written permission from the authors, keep it open; (b) move to proprietary/ and accept that history retains the blob; (c) move to proprietary/ and purge from history, which rewrites public history; (d) keep only the metadata and citation in open/, drop the PDF.

notes.author: teddy0@snrsi-arch-desktop
notes.content:
MAINTAINER DECISION 2026-08-14: keep it in open/. Grounds given: Anders Choo and Sicong Xiao are the maintainer's own colleagues at SNRSI.

Recorded rather than assumed -- the catalogue entry now carries a 'Tier decision' note stating that this is a DELIBERATE EXCEPTION to the workspace default (no licence statement means proprietary), who made it, and on what grounds.

The note also records the caveat the maintainer was given and accepted: no written grant is on file, and the copyright asserted on the INIS record is the IAEA's rather than the authors'. VINANST-15 is conference proceedings, whose copyright is commonly assigned to the organiser, so a permission from the authors would not by itself settle the redistribution right. If an explicit grant is ever obtained, the note says to upgrade it naming who granted it and when.

STILL OPEN, and unrelated to the tier: the same document exists twice under two tiers and two years. Filed separately as a cleanup chore.

title: LICENCE: choo2023criticality is in open/ and committed to a public repo, but carries no redistribution grant

description:
Recorded as a PROPOSAL for the maintainer to decide. Do not execute a deletion from this bead.

crates/outram-park-fork-coolprop/src/openfoam_algorithms/ is 18,016 lines across 96 .rs files that duplicate crates/outram-foam-basic-lib, and the copies have diverged.

Measured divergence (coolprop copy vs basic-lib counterpart, diff lines):
  fv_operators/fvm/laplacian.rs      163 vs  771   (688 diff)
  primitives/tensor.rs               764 vs 1053   (559)
  ode/rkf45.rs                       299 vs  333   ( 88)
  thermophysics/eos/peng_robinson.rs 465 vs  482   ( 91)
  polynomial/cubic_eqn.rs            247 vs  268   ( 47)
  math/erf_inv.rs                     79 vs   84   (  9)
Concrete example: fvm/laplacian.rs has ONE public fn in both, but basic-lib has grown ~4.7x (non-orthogonal correction / boundary handling) that the copy never received. At the other end, erf_inv.rs differs by 9 lines of pure rustfmt -- so the copies are drifting both semantically and cosmetically.

TWO CORRECTIONS that make a naive deletion unsafe:
1. It is NOT dead code. lib.rs:150 `pub mod openfoam_algorithms;` and lib.rs:156 `pub use openfoam_algorithms::rhoPimpleFoam::{OPCPFluidArray, OPCPFluidArrayError};`. Deleting the directory removes public API from a published crate.
2. It is a THREE-way duplication. lib.rs:146-147 records that the module was copied from tampines-steam-tables, and crates/tampines-steam-tables/src/ holds its own 20,696-line, 101-file openfoam copy. Cargo.toml:29 explicitly records "no outram-foam-basic-lib dependency -- the primitives are vendored", so the duplication was DELIBERATE.

Any proposal must therefore address all three copies and revisit the deliberate no-dependency decision, and handle the public-API break (semver).

Verified 2026-08-07.
title: PROPOSAL: de-duplicate the 3-way vendored OpenFOAM layer (coolprop / steam-tables / basic-lib)
